Karthik —

Thanks for sending this over. We reviewed Exhibit B with procurement and finance. A few immediate concerns:

1) An 8% unconditional holdback is a non-starter for our auditors — it impacts revenue recognition and creates cashflow mismatch for our internal vendors.
2) We can consider a conditional holdback if it is capped at 4% and tied to a short release schedule (e.g., monthly release following a 60-day reconciliation window).
3) We need clearer definitions for "cap" and "floor" in the pricing schedule — specifically how credits and usage true-ups feed into the monthly invoice.

I've attached a marked-up PDF with inline comments (AeroMed_Orderform_marked.pdf). Main edits are: replace 8% with 4%, define the escrow release (60/30 split), and an explicit exception paragraph for PHI-handled workloads (we accept carveouts but want explicit routing obligations).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a time-limited holdback (12 months) and whether you can add an alternative mechanism: a reconciliation credit in lieu of holdback if we can provide a forecast and a rolling 30-day true-up?

Regards,

Karthik / Marissa —

Quick legal read of AeroMed's marked PDF. Goal: keep Commercial moving while limiting legal risk. Proposed approach:

- Compromise holdback: 6% phased (Month 1: 6% withheld; Months 2–3: 4% withheld; after Month 3: full release contingent on no outstanding true-up disputes).
- Sunset: 12-month automatic termination of holdback unless both parties agree in writing to extend.
- Carveouts: explicit defini tions for "Regulated Workload" (PHI/PHI-adjacent) — Redwood will not apply holdback to workloads delivered under Dedicated/Private pricing (Exhibit D). Add routing obligation: customer must identify regulated workloads via the onboarding checklist within first 30 days or they remain subject to holdback.
- Fee ceiling/floor: add a short Exhibit B Appendix that defines monthly fee ceiling (max invoiced tokens) and floor (minimum committed token spend) with a reconciliation formula. This avoids open-ended phrasing that finance flags.

Suggested redline snippet for Section 4.2 (Fee Holdback):
"During the first three billing cycles following Effective Date, Customer's monthly invoice shall reflect a temporary holdback equal to 6% of the Monthly Committed Fees (the \"Holdback\"). The Holdback shall be released in equal installments following each monthly reconciliation provided that any outstanding usage true-ups or disputed charges are resolved. The Holdback shall automatically expire 12 months after the Effective Date unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing. Regulated Workloads, as defined in Exhibit D, are excluded from the Holdback."

If Procurement insists on 4% escrow, we should present the phased 6% as a commercial compromise — gives room to move later without reopening the entire orderform.

I can drop these redlines into v4 and circulate. Also recommend adding an explicit billing contact block to Exhibit B for invoicing cadence and dispute resolution timelines.

Laura Bennett
